claim: Vitamin D deficiency prevails in epidemic proportions across the Indian subcontinent, with 70-100% prevalence in the general healthy population, according to this comprehensive 2014 review.
stance_target: Vitamin D deficiency affects the overwhelming majority of Indians, making supplementation broadly necessary
scope_conditions: India and Indian subcontinent; healthy general population across all regions, ages, and demographics; multiple studies
quoted_support: Vitamin D deficiency prevails in epidemic proportions all over the Indian subcontinent, with a prevalence of 70%–100% in the general population.

claim: Indian dairy products are rarely fortified with vitamin D, and Indian socioreligious and cultural practices do not facilitate adequate sun exposure, negating the benefit of plentiful sunshine.
stance_target: Dietary and cultural factors in India create structural, irreversible drivers of vitamin D deficiency requiring supplementation
quoted_support: In India, widely consumed food items such as dairy products are rarely fortified with vitamin D. Indian socioreligious and cultural practices do not facilitate adequate sun exposure, thereby negating potential benefits of plentiful sunshine.

claim: Vitamin D deficiency was documented in most of 2,119 healthcare professionals studied from all over India, demonstrating the deficiency is universal across socioeconomic and occupational groups.
stance_target: Vitamin D deficiency is not a problem of poverty or poor access alone — it affects educated, health-aware professionals
quoted_support: Vitamin D deficiency was also observed in most of 2119 healthcare professionals studied from all over India. Evidently, countrywide prevalence of vitamin D deficiency is undeniable.

claim: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is preferred over vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) for supplementation, as cholecalciferol is the natural form produced by skin on sun exposure.
stance_target: Cholecalciferol-based supplements like Briyo's D3 2000 IU are the scientifically preferred form for supplementation
quoted_support: Commercially, vitamin D3 is manufactured by ultraviolet irradiation of 7-dehydrocholesterol from lanolin. Both forms of vitamin D are available as vitamin D supplements.

claim: Vitamin D deficiency is associated with 30-50% increased risk of developing and dying from colorectal, prostate, breast, pancreatic, and esophageal cancer when 25(OH)D levels are below 20 ng/mL.
stance_target: Extraskeletal benefits of vitamin D supplementation extend to cancer prevention, supporting broader health claims
scope_conditions: Global; retrospective and prospective epidemiological studies
quoted_support: Retrospective and prospective epidemiologic studies showed that when 25(OH)D levels were <20 ng/mL there was a 30%–50% increased risk of developing and dying of colorectal, prostate, breast, pancreatic, and esophageal cancer.

claim: Meta-analysis showed a 30% reduction in risk of Type 1 diabetes in children receiving vitamin D supplements, and combined calcium + vitamin D supplementation benefits insulin resistance and hyperglycemia.
stance_target: Vitamin D supplementation has documented preventive benefits for metabolic and autoimmune conditions beyond bone health
quoted_support: A meta-analysis of observational studies showed a 30% reduction in risk of T1D in children receiving vitamin D supplements.
